correctness.rationale: Exact centered vertex norm identity gives a finite contact family. The rearrangement inequality yields C_min=(n−1)(−n(n−5)/12+λ+λ²/n). When C_min≤0, two symmetry-averaged contact orbits mix to isotropic covariance R²/(2n−2)I, and the trace/AM–GM bound proves the circumball is the globally unique minimum-volume ellipsoid. When C_min>0, Q_ε=||u||²+||v||²−2εu·v yields an explicitly strict smaller-volume enclosing ellipsoid for sufficiently small ε. The criterion covers all integer n≥2 and real λ>0 including equality. A rational checker independently tests finite cases; no finite check is treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The known Euclidean circumsphere does not solve the stronger minimum-volume enclosing-ellipsoid problem because diagonal-permutation symmetry permits two inequivalent covariance modes. The sharp λ_c(n) threshold and n=7 canonical onset identify a structural geometry phase transition and give explicit positive isotropic contact-frame weights or a strict anisotropic competitor on opposing sides. The critical λ scale is n^{3/2} and differs from prior weighted-inball behavior; the result is a natural whole-family classification rather than a numerical slice.
